subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Herringbone Gears: Canceling Thrust
description: A quick, practical guide to Herringbone Gears: Canceling Thrust.

hook.text: Helical gears run smooth but push sideways. Herringbone gears use two opposing helixes to cancel that thrust.

buildup.text: A herringbone gear has V-shaped teeth — two helical patterns mirrored on one gear face.

discovery.text: The opposing angles generate equal and opposite axial forces. They cancel perfectly, leaving pure torque.

twist.text: They're expensive to machine. A groove in the middle separates the two helixes because cutting a true V is hard.

climax.text: Ship turbines and large power plant gearboxes use herringbone gears. High cost is justified by massive loads.

punchline.text: Mirror the helix. Kill the thrust. Elegance costs extra.

quiz.question: How do herringbone gears eliminate axial thrust?
options: They use special bearings to absorb the sideways force
Two opposing helical tooth patterns generate equal and opposite thrust forces
The teeth are coated with low-friction material that prevents sliding
